When scoring a competition, the main purpose of “removing 1 highest score and 1 lowest score, then calculating the mean” is to ( ).

choices.A: Reduce the influence of individual extreme scores

displayedInputs.question: The weekly pocket money amounts (in yuan) for 6 students in a class are 10, 10, 15, 15, 20, 50. By how many yuan does the mean exceed the median?
What are the range and variance of the data 2, 4, 6? (Write the range followed by the variance, expressing the variance as a fraction.)
What is the range of the data 12, 5, 9, 20, 3?
What is the variance of the data 1, 3, 5, 7?
Groups A and B have the same mean. Group A has a standard deviation of 1.5, and Group B has a variance of 2. Which group has less variability (is more stable)? ( )
A data set has a variance of 3. If every data value is multiplied by 2, what is the variance of the new data set?

For the data 1 through 8, find the first and third quartiles using the method of taking the median of each half of the data. (The data are 1, 2, …, 8. Write the first quartile followed by the third quartile, separated by a comma.)
What is the second quartile (the median) of the data 2, 4, 6, 8?

For the sorted data 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 14, 15, find the interquartile range (the third quartile minus the first quartile; take the median of the first 4 values and the median of the last 4 values separately).

The sorted data are 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11, 12 (7 values in total). When the number of data values is odd, exclude the median itself, then take the medians of the lower 3 values and the upper 3 values to obtain the first and third quartiles. Find the interquartile range.
A larger interquartile range indicates that ( ).

choices.A: The middle 50% of the data are more spread out.
choices.B: The middle 50% of the data are more concentrated.
choices.C: The mean of the data is larger.

displayedInputs.question: How can the mean be estimated from grouped data?

choices.A: Add the class midpoints and divide by the number of classes.
choices.B: Add the class frequencies and divide by the number of classes.
choices.C: Multiply each class's upper limit by its frequency, add the products, and divide by the total frequency.
choices.D: Multiply each class midpoint by its frequency, add the products, and divide by the total frequency.

displayedInputs.question: A class interval for a data set is 20 to 30. What is the class midpoint?
The frequencies of the classes 0 to 10, 10 to 20, and 20 to 30 are 3, 5, and 2, respectively. What is the estimated mean of this data set using the class midpoints?
The frequencies of the classes 40 to 50, 50 to 60, 60 to 70, and 70 to 80 are 4, 10, 16, and 10, respectively. What is the estimated mean using the class midpoints?
Which statement correctly compares the mean estimated using class midpoints with the actual mean of the original data? ( )

choices.B: There may be an error because the specific data values within each class are lost after grouping.
choices.C: The estimated mean must be too high.

displayedInputs.question: How should the physical fitness test scores of two classes be compared?

choices.A: Compare only the highest score in each class.
choices.B: Compare only the number of students in each class.
choices.C: Use the mean to compare overall performance and the variance to compare consistency.
choices.D: Compare only the lowest score in each class.

displayedInputs.question: The numbers of rope skips completed in 1 minute by 5 students in a class are 120, 130, 140, 150, and 160. How many skips did each student complete on average?
The physical fitness test scores of 5 students sampled from Class A are 80, 82, 78, 84, and 76, with a mean of 80. Find the variance.
To learn about the physical fitness of all 1200 students in a school, which sampling plan is the most reasonable? ( )

choices.A: Randomly select some students from each grade level.
choices.B: Select only students on the school's track and field team.
